items.q: If twice as many workers do a job, what happens to the time?
hints: In inverse proportion, one quantity doubling makes the other quantity half as much.
Twice the workers means the job is shared out more, so it takes half the time.
It halves

items.q: If the number of people triples, what happens to the time in inverse proportion?
hints: In inverse proportion, multiplying one quantity by a number divides the other by the same number.
Tripling the people means the time is divided by 3.
It becomes a third

items.q: 4 workers take 6 hours. In inverse proportion, how long do 8 workers take?
hints: In inverse proportion, workers x time stays constant.
4 x 6 = 24, so 8 x time = 24.

items.q: 5 taps fill a tank in 12 minutes. How long would 10 taps take in inverse proportion?
hints: In inverse proportion, taps x time stays constant.

items.q: True or false: in inverse proportion, one quantity increases while the other decreases.
hints: Recall the defining behaviour of inverse proportion.
As one variable grows, the other shrinks so that their product stays constant.
True

items.q: 3 people take 20 minutes. How long would 1 person take in inverse proportion?
hints: In inverse proportion, people x time stays constant.
3 x 20 = 60, so 1 x time = 60.

items.q: 6 machines complete a job in 10 hours. How long would 4 machines take, in inverse proportion?
hints: In inverse proportion, machines x time stays constant.
6 x 10 = 60, so 4 x time = 60.
